# Data exploration: joint indices, census and catch reconstruction (JARA)

JABBA3 includes the data-exploration models of JARA, refitted in RTMB: a
state-space random walk with drift on log abundance (or log catch), observed
through one or several series. JARA and JABBA build the assessment story
together:

1. **catch reconstruction**: fill missing years in landings by country or fleet
   with the series-specific trends (census model) and sum them to a total catch
   with uncertainty;
2. **joint index**: combine several noisy surveys or CPUE series with different
   time spans into one relative abundance index, following the hierarchical
   analysis of multiple noisy abundance indices of Conn (2010) that is widely
   used in SEDAR assessments; JARA's relative joint index reproduces Conn's
   approach, and JABBA3 offers both forms (random walk, `state = "rw"`, and
   Conn's independent year effects, `state = "iid"`);
3. **assessment**: feed both into `jabba3()`, the joint index as the single
   index with its log-scale SE, the filled catch with a year-specific catch SE.

The model, for series $i$ in year $t$:

$$x_t = x_{t-1} + r_{b(t)} + \eta_t,\quad \eta_t \sim N(0, \sigma_p^2);\qquad
\log I_{i,t} = \log q_i + x_t + \varepsilon_{i,t},\quad
\varepsilon_{i,t} \sim N(0, se_{i,t}^2 + \sigma_{fix}^2 + \sigma_i^2)$$

- `type = "relative"`: one common state, $q_1 = 1$, the other $q_i$ estimated
  (joint index);
- `type = "census"`: one state per series with $q = 1$ (absolute catch or
  abundance by country, fleet or area), summed to a total;
- `timeblock`: the drift $r_{b(t)}$ differs before and after the block year,
  so missing values are interpolated with the block-specific trend;
- `variance.weighting`: `"model"` estimates the additional SD $\sigma_i$ by
  series, `"equal"` one common value, `"fixed"` none; `fixed.obsE` is
  $\sigma_{fix}$.

The fits use the JABBA3 diagnostics (fits, runs test, residuals, posterior
predictive checks). As everywhere in JABBA3, residual plots default to
one-step-ahead (OSA) residuals; `type = "ordinary"` gives the log residuals
used in JARA reports.

```{r jara-data}
data(jara_examples)
names(jara_examples)
```

The Dentex landings are those printed in the 2025 BCC catch reconstruction; the
survey indices are illustrative (simulated with the same structure as the
monkfish surveys). The original files (catchDentex2025.csv, cpueMonk2025.csv,
idxMonk2025.csv) can replace them directly.

## Step 1: catch reconstruction (census with a time block)

Dentex landings from Namibia (NAM) and Angola (ANG). Angola did not report in
several years between 1985 and 1994; the low landings from Namibia in
2009-2011 and from Angola in 2012 are incomplete and treated as unobserved
(NA). The series start in 1976, so the interpolation infers the decline up to
1992; a time block at 1992 lets the trend after 1992 differ (recovery).

```{r jara-dentex-raw, fig.height = 3.5}
den <- jara_examples$dentex
head(den)
L <- den[den$year >= 1976, ]
dl <- rbind(data.frame(year = L$year, country = "NAM", landings = L$NAM),
            data.frame(year = L$year, country = "ANG", landings = L$ANG))
ggplot2::ggplot(dl, ggplot2::aes(year, landings, colour = country)) + ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) + ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 1992, linetype = 2) + theme_jabba3()
```

`jb3_catchfill()` fits the census model to both series (known landings with an
observation SD of 0.001, as JARA's `fixed.obsE = 0.001`):

```{r jara-dentex-fit, fig.height = 4}
cf <- jb3_catchfill(L, se = 0.001, timeblock = 1992)
cfit <- attr(cf, "fit")
cfit                                   # drift before and after the block
jbplot_trend(cfit)                     # series fits and the total with 95% intervals
```

Missing years carry high uncertainty, which propagates into the total:

```{r jara-dentex-total, fig.height = 3.5}
jbplot_catchfill(cf)
```

The reconstructed table: original series with the NAs replaced by predictions,
and the total (cf. Table 1 of the Dentex report):

```{r jara-dentex-table}
tab <- jb3_fill_table(cf, digits = 1)
knitr::kable(tab[tab$year %in% c(1983:1995, 2007:2014), ], row.names = FALSE)
```

## Step 2: joint survey index

Three surveys with different time spans and gaps (WC from 1985, SC from 1988,
NAM from 1999). As in the monkfish analysis, the indices are first normalised by
their means, and the joint index is fitted with equal and with model-estimated
(inverse-variance) weighting:

```{r jara-surveys-raw, fig.height = 3.5}
srv <- jara_examples$surveys
srv.n <- srv; for(v in names(srv)[-1]) srv.n[[v]] <- srv[[v]]/mean(srv[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
dsv <- stats::reshape(srv.n, direction = "long", varying = names(srv.n)[-1], v.names = "index",
                      timevar = "survey", times = names(srv.n)[-1], idvar = "year")
ggplot2::ggplot(dsv, ggplot2::aes(year, index, colour = survey)) + ggplot2::geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) + theme_jabba3()
```

```{r jara-surveys-fit}
ji.eq  <- jb3_trend(srv.n, variance.weighting = "equal", run = "equal")
ji.mod <- jb3_trend(srv.n, variance.weighting = "model", run = "model")
rbind(equal = ji.eq$sdi, model = ji.mod$sdi)        # additional observation SD by survey
```

Diagnostics of the model-weighted fit: fits and runs tests, the joint residual
plot for data conflicts, and posterior predictive checks with Bayesian
p-values (near 0.5 under a well-specified model):

```{r jara-surveys-diag, fig.height = 3.5}
jbplot_fits(ji.mod)
jbplot_runs(ji.mod, type = "ordinary")
```

```{r jara-surveys-resid, fig.height = 4}
jbplot_residuals(ji.mod, type = "ordinary")
p <- jbplot_ppc(ji.mod); attr(p, "ppc")
```

The joint index: the precision-weighted mean of the q-scaled surveys by year
with its log-scale SE (NA in years without a survey, as in JARA; `fill = TRUE`
fills them with the state), and the state-space trend (red dashed). The two
weightings give nearly the same joint index here:

```{r jara-surveys-joint, fig.height = 3.5}
jbplot_jointindex(ji.mod)
ji <- jb3_jointindex(ji.mod)
ji.cmp <- data.frame(year = ji$year, equal = jb3_jointindex(ji.eq)$index, model = ji$index)
round(cor(ji.cmp$equal, ji.cmp$model, use = "complete.obs"), 3)
knitr::kable(head(ji, 10), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

**Random walk (JARA) or independent year effects (Conn 2010).** Conn's model
estimates the log joint index as independent year effects,
$\log U_{it} \sim N(n_t + c_i, \sigma_{p,i}^2 + \sigma_{s,it}^2)$ with
$n_t \sim N(\bar n, 1)$, the same observation model as above with
`variance.weighting = "model"`; JARA's default links the years by the random
walk. Where the indices overlap, the two give practically the same joint index:

```{r jara-conn, fig.height = 3.5}
ji.conn <- jb3_trend(srv.n, state = "iid", run = "Conn (iid)")
jc <- jb3_jointindex(ji.conn)
ok <- is.finite(ji$index) & is.finite(jc$index)
cmp <- data.frame(year = ji$year[ok], rw = ji$index[ok]/mean(ji$index[ok]), iid = jc$index[ok]/mean(jc$index[ok]))
round(c(correlation = cor(log(cmp$rw), log(cmp$iid)), max.rel.diff = max(abs(cmp$rw/cmp$iid - 1))), 3)
ggplot2::ggplot(cmp, ggplot2::aes(year)) + ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = rw, colour = "random walk (JARA)")) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(y = iid, colour = "iid (Conn 2010)")) + ggplot2::labs(y = "Joint index", colour = NULL) +
  theme_jabba3()
```

The independent-year-effects form needs overlapping indices to scale them
against each other: for series that do not overlap in time (e.g. the early and
late bigeye longline CPUE) only the random walk links them, through the
continuity of the state.

## Step 3: into the JABBA3 assessment

The reconstructed catch goes into `jb3_data()` with its year-specific
log-scale SE, which the catch error of the model uses in place of the constant
`sdc` (reconstructed years carry more catch error than fully reported years);
the joint index goes in as the single index, its `log.se` as the SE:

```{r jara-into-jabba3}
d <- jb3_data(cf, ji, stock = "illustrative")
round(range(d$catch.se), 3)
fit <- jabba3(d, jb3_priors(d, r = c(0.4, 0.3)), jb3_model(shape = "schaefer"), run = "JARA -> JABBA3")
fit
```

```{r jara-into-jabba3-plot, fig.height = 9, fig.width = 10}
plot(fit)
```

The joint index is also available as an `FLIndexBiomass` with `index.var` =
log.se (`jb3_jointindex(ji.mod, "FLIndexBiomass")`) for FLR workflows, and
year-specific catch uncertainty can also be given directly with
`jb3_data(..., catch.se =)` or a vector `sdc` in `jb3_model()`.

## Further examples

**Two CPUE series (anglerfish).** The last 17 years of the Portuguese and
Spanish anglerfish CPUE from the JARA joint-index report; the input SEs are very
small (about 0.07), so an additional fixed observation error of 0.1 is added:

```{r jara-ank, fig.height = 3.5}
ank <- jara_examples$ank
for(v in c("POR", "ESP")) ank[[v]] <- ank[[v]]/mean(ank[[v]][ank$year > 2009], na.rm = TRUE)
ank.fit <- jb3_trend(ank, jara_examples$ank.se, fixed.obsE = 0.1, run = "ANK")
jbplot_jointindex(ank.fit)
```

**Census of survey areas.** With absolute abundance indices (swept-area
biomass, acoustic surveys) from different areas, `type = "census"` sums the
area states to a total biomass with uncertainty, an absolute index for the
assessment:

```{r jara-census, fig.height = 5}
set.seed(3); yrs <- 1990:2020
tru <- sapply(c(100, 50, 30), function(a) a*exp(cumsum(c(0, rnorm(30, -0.01, 0.1)))))
obs <- tru*exp(matrix(rnorm(length(tru), 0, 0.2), ncol = 3)); obs[sample(length(obs), 20)] <- NA
cen.fit <- jb3_trend(data.frame(year = yrs, A = obs[, 1], B = obs[, 2], C = obs[, 3]),
                     data.frame(year = yrs, A = 0.2, B = 0.2, C = 0.2), type = "census", variance.weighting = "fixed")
jbplot_trend(cen.fit)
```

**Log-scale standard errors.** From a design-based SD of the untransformed
index, use $CV = sd/mean$ and $\sigma = \sqrt{\log(CV^2 + 1)}$ (close to the CV
for CV < 0.4); from a 95% interval, $\sigma = (\log(uci) - \log(lci))/(2 \times 1.96)$.
